newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey says Kurdish holiday celebrations allowed.
newsitem.headline: Turkey says Kurdish holiday celebrations allowed.

text.p: Turkey said on Thursday it would allow the celebration of a Kurdish holiday later this month but warned against traditional displays of separatism.
"Newroz can be celebrated freely by everyone as long as there are no ideological motives," regional governor Necati Bilican told reporters in the southeastern city of Batman.
The Newroz festival on March 21 is regarded by Kurds as a traditional day of protest. Dozens of civilians died at Newroz in 1992 in clashes between demonstrators and security forces.
Bilican said officials would take precautions against attacks by Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) rebels around the holidays.
More than 21,000 people have died in 12 years of conflict between troops and the PKK, fighting for independence or autonomy in southeast Turkey.
Authorities allowed some public celebrations of Newroz last year but a moderate Kurdish political party was banned from marking the event with street demonstrations.

The People's Democracy Party (HADEP) said it had received permission to mark the festival with rallies in major cities in western Turkey this year but had yet to be given the go-ahead for celebrations in the mainly Kurdish southeast.
